newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvest begins but lags average.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvest begins but lags average.

text.p: Saskatchewan's spring crop harvest began but lagged the five-year average in the week ended August 26, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in a report.

About 31 percent of spring cereals were ripe, 40 percent of canola, seven percent of flax and 44 percent of pulse crops were ripe. Eighty percent of fall rye and 73 percent of winter wheat was combined.
Combining of spring crops was behind the five-year average with 39 percent of spring rye, four percent of canola, three percent of barley, two percent of wheat and oats in the bin.
An average 10 mm of rain fell across the province.

Southern Saskatchewan saw an average 12 mm of rain with a high of 50 mm (two inches) near Odessa. Five to 40 percent of fields in the Estevan region saw hail damage. Drought stress was reported around Estevan, Swift Current and Maple Creek.
Central Saskatchewan saw an average 13 mm of rain with a high of 60 mm (2.4 inches) near Langenburg. Frost was reported south of Wilkie in the west. Heat and drought stress was reported in the west.
Northern Saskatchewan saw less than one mm of rain. Hail damage was reported around Humboldt. Heat and drought stress was reported in the west.
